slides.0.title: Regulatory depth and reading labels
slides.0.subtitle: Klassik/Reserve, Ried and Wachau
slides.1.title: Threshold comparison
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Grüner/Riesling DACs
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Weinviertel, Kremstal, Kamptal, Traisental: Klassik at least 12%, Reserve at least 13%
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Blaufränkisch DACs
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Mittelburgenland, Eisenberg: Klassik 12.5–13%, Reserve at least 13%
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Wien
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Klassik at most 12.5% and Ried at least 12.5% (opposite directions)
slides.1.content: Diploma questions often ask for a DAC's threshold: learn Klassik and Reserve separately.
slides.2.title: Ried and label reading
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Tiers
slides.2.highlights.0.content: A village name (Ortswein) or Ried name (Riedenwein) means a narrower origin, while Gebietswein shows only the region
slides.2.highlights.1.title: DAC versus non-DAC
slides.2.highlights.1.content: A wine labelled with the variety and Qualitätswein but no DAC region name has usually opted out of DAC rules
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Prädikat conditions
slides.2.highlights.2.content: A must-weigher's confirmation is required, with no enrichment or sweetening
slides.2.content: Read a label in this order: region → tier → variety → style term (Klassik/Reserve/Prädikat).
slides.3.title: Wachau Codex alongside DAC
slides.3.highlights.0.title: Two vocabularies
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Steinfeder/Federspiel/Smaragd are Vinea Wachau's trademarked grades, while Gebietswein/Ortswein/Riedenwein are the DAC's statutory tiers
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Details of coexistence
slides.3.highlights.1.content: The exact way the two coexist was not checked against official documents; verify against Vinea Wachau and ÖWM rules before an exam
slides.3.content: First separate the two ideas: an association trademark versus a statutory tier.
What kind of system are Steinfeder/Federspiel/Smaragd?
The three grades are Vinea Wachau trademarks.
In Wien, how do the Klassik and Ried alcohol rules run?
A. Klassik a floor, Ried a cap
C. Klassik at most 12.5%, Ried at least 12.5%
Klassik is a cap and Ried a floor.
When may Spätlese earliest be submitted for the state test number?
A. October of the harvest year
Spätlese and Auslese from 1 January, other Prädikat wines from 1 April.
